newsitem.title: HONG KONG: High HK land auction prices point to bullishness.
newsitem.headline: High HK land auction prices point to bullishness.

text.p: Two Hong Kong residential sites fetched above-expectation prices in a Wednesday government land auction despite concerns of a possible clampdown on speculation, indicating bullishness in the market, analysts said.

The key plot, a 2008 square metre site in Repulse Bay on the south side of Hong Kong island slated for luxury residential purposes, sold for HK$230 million (US$29.7 million) indicating an accommodation value of HK$18,357 per square foot.
Analysts and property consultants had forecast it would sell for between HK$179 million and HK$188 million.

A 5,080 square metre site in Tuen Mun in the New Territories sold for HK$258 million, representing an accommodation value of HK$3,629 psf. Property consultants had expected the plot for residential usage to fetch HK$178 million to HK$200 million.
Both sites attracted about seven bidders each, and eventually went to Eton Properties Development Co Ltd, government land agent Francis Ng told reporters.
"The result is slightly higher than what we expected," Ng said. "I think people are having great confidence in the market and they look for more investment opportunities."
"I think the market is strong. People have keen demand for premises," he added.
"That was definitely aggressive pricing," said Desmond Cheung at Vickers Ballas Hong Kong. He said the results also fuelled price rises in property stocks.
Tony Chan, managing director at Ricacorp Surveyors Ltd, said the results showed developers were bullish about the market.
He also attributed the high pricing to a shortage of supply of developable land, particularly on Hong Kong island.

"This is very positive," said Martin Tacon, senior associate at CS First Boston. "On the basis of what they have paid for the project that is a definite indication that they think luxury residential prices on the south side are going to go up."
Vickers' Ng attributed the high price for the Repulse Bay site partly to the recent great demand for luxury residence.
Grace Woo, Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd executive director and general manager, property investment and valuation, said the site's pricing reflected an optimistic sentiment.
"You saw quite a lot of competition for the site," she said.
Chan said the development at the Repulse Bay site was expected to sell in 1999 at 23,000 or 24,000 per square foot, at a 15 percent premium to current prices.

The project at the Tuen Mun plot would sell at over HK$6,000 per square fott, about 25 to 30 percent above current prices, Chan said. "The price will positively affect the middle-to-low residential sector," he said.

But Cheung and other analysts noted the two plots were relatively small in value and size and may not indicate an overall trend, saying they would rather wait for more clues from flat sales for a clearer view of the market.

Ng said he was not worried that the strong bidding will fuel further speculation. If the sites were intended for long-term development and needs and not for immediate supply, then there would not be a serious effect, he said.
Analysts said concerns over government's possible anti-speculative measures did not affect the auction results.
"Judging from today's auction results, that didn't have an impact on developers. They appeared to be still keen," Chan said.
